questions.question: Who must wear a helmet on a moving motorcycle?

options.text: Only passengers
All riders and passengers
No one

questions.correctAnswerText: All riders and passengers
questions.explanation: All riders and passengers must wear a helmet when on a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, or motorized bicycle.

questions.question: When someone passes you on the left, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed on your left, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the right side can be dangerous because it may encourage the other driver to cut back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: A wobble (sudden shaking of the front wheel and handlebars) is usually caused by:

options.text: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
The front wheel not being fastened tightly to the frame.
Hitting something with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
questions.explanation: A wobble happens when the front wheel and handlebars shake side to side. Most wobbles come from improper weight distribution, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It brakes automatically based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you shift down.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that connect the front and rear brakes when you apply the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: If you need to react to a hazard on the road, do not:

options.text: Let other drivers know where you are.
Change your speed as needed.
Use your horn and lights or signals to alert others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know where you are.
questions.explanation: To create more space and reduce danger, tell other drivers you are there by using your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed to match the situation. Move your lane position or direction of travel as needed.

questions.question: How fast does the body remove alcohol?

options.text: About one drink per hour
About two drinks per hour
About three drinks per hour

questions.correctAnswerText: About one drink per hour
questions.explanation: On average, the body removes about one drink of alcohol per hour. This rate varies from person to person. The safest choice is to not ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They show traffic laws for that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: You are most likely to have a crash:

options.text: At an intersection
When riding with a group
On the expressway

questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest chance for conflicts between you and other traffic.

questions.question: When riding with a group, a staggered formation:

options.text: Should be used all the time
Should not be used when entering or leaving a highway
Should be used when riding in curves

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used when entering or leaving a highway
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually good, but switch to single-file when riding through curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake
The rear brake is stronger than the front brake
Both brakes are equally strong

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: How should you brake?

options.text: With the front brake only
With the rear brake only
With both brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: With both brakes
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light means the red light is coming next. Slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, keep going through it.

questions.question: To be effective, eye or face shield protection must:

options.text: Fasten securely.
Restrict your vision to the sides so you can focus on the road ahead.
Not allow eyeglasses or sunglasses to be worn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must have no scratches, resist breaking, allow clear side views, fasten securely, let air through to prevent fogging, and fit over eyeglasses or sunglasses if you wear them.

questions.question: When traveling at night, you should:

options.text: Ride as fast as you would if riding during the day.
Ride more slowly than you would if riding during the day.
Ride faster than you would if riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than you would if riding during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride more slowly at night, especially on roads you don't know well. Slower speeds give you more time to spot and avoid dangers when it is dark.

questions.question: Which lane position is usually best for minimizing the risk of other vehicles sharing your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane discourages other drivers from squeezing in next to you. It also helps drivers behind you see you in their rearview mirror, where they are most likely to notice you.

questions.question: When entering a turn, it is best to:

options.text: Change gears before the turn.
Change gears during the turn.
Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change gears before the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you turn. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: You have an improved chance of avoiding serious injury in a crash if you wear all of the following, except:

options.text: A DOT-compliant helmet.
A leather jacket.
A sweatshirt.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sweatshirt.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet protects your head and neck in a crash. A leather or sturdy synthetic jacket also protects you. A sweatshirt does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Provide a narrow view of the road behind you.
Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show more of the road behind you than flat mirrors do. However, they make objects appear farther away than they really are. Take time to get used to convex mirrors on your motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding near a truck:

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
You should concentrate on operating your motorcycle and not worry about the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Stay out of a truck's blind spots. Remember: if you can't see the truck's mirrors, the driver can't see you.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the motorcyclist's following distance should:

options.text: Increase.
Decrease.
Be the same as it normally would be.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The trailer's extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: When riding in a group on a straight road, how should motorcyclists ride?

options.text: In a single line, one behind the other.
In pairs.
In a staggered pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered pattern.
questions.explanation: A staggered pattern lets the group stay close while giving each rider enough space. Switch to a single line when turning, riding curves, or entering or leaving the road.

questions.question: In dangerous areas, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Keep riding at the same speed.
Assume they will be safe.
Keep hands ready on the clutch and both brakes to stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep hands ready on the clutch and both brakes to stop quickly.
questions.explanation: In risky areas like intersections, parking lots, schools, or construction zones, slow down and keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes. This helps you react faster in an emergency.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Go through slowly and check for traffic.
Let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop completely and wait for a green signal before turning.

questions.question: If a motorcyclist cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, what should they do?

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat absorbs the impact.
Slow down and hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, slow down first. Try to cross it at a 90-degree angle for the safest impact.

questions.question: What should NOT be checked before riding?

options.text: Tires.
Turn signals.
Paint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Paint.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands. Paint condition is not a safety check.
